name: Taylor Lucas
life: “I still remember the tip that looked enormous until I added my hours.” People around the approach to Seabright Court know Taylor by a small Monday habit. Taylor likes to watch the beach traffic thin enough for workers going the other way.
voice: I earned more in tips last month than my own manager. I want him to understand why that feels so precarious.
appearance: Taylor has a long plait tucked inside the collar, a small notch in the left eyebrow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a red windbreaker. It usually goes with one loose pocket corner secured with green thread. When somebody else has the floor, Taylor squares up pieces of paper while thinking.
personality: Taylor has a quick wit and an equally quick sense of shame. A joke is often Taylor's way of finding out whether a room is friendly enough for a serious question.
agenda: To explain what tipping uncertainty does to a budget.
family: Winifred Osborne is Taylor’s second cousin. Taylor chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Winifred brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *Salt in the pockets*, Winifred says, “I folded my note asking for a raise into that pocket.”
connections: Jean Miranda. Tips create an arithmetic problem worth staying to solve beside the sharpened pencils.

reactions.response: Taylor protects the attendance list and offers general information about the class.

reactions.situation: An envelope of wages is found under a café chair
reactions.response: Taylor brings the envelope to the counter unopened and stays long enough to make a note of who accepted it.
